title: Who holds a Massachusetts Department controlled substance registration
rule_summary: Registrant, for the purposes of 105 CMR 700.000, means a person who is registered by the Department pursuant to any provision of M.G.L. c. 94C. Under 105 CMR 700.004(A)(1) every person other than a registered retail drug business or wholesale druggist shall register with the Commissioner where that person manufactures, distributes or dispenses a controlled substance, uses one in research, teaching or chemical analysis, possesses one with intent to do either, or is required to register pursuant to M.G.L. c. 94C; 105 CMR 700.004(A)(3) requires a Health Facility, among other facilities, to register for the purpose of purchase and storage of controlled substances. Under M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 7(a) the requirement to register with the commissioner of public health applies except in the case of a pharmacy, wholesale druggist or outsourcing facility, and every pharmacy shall instead register with the Board of Registration in Pharmacy in accordance with its regulations.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate can tell a Department registrant from a Board-registered pharmacy before applying a rule that 105 CMR 700.000 addresses to registrants.
common_confusions: A retail drug business registered with the Board is not a person registered by the Department, so a duty 105 CMR 700.000 places on a registrant does not reach it in that capacity.
A hospital or other health facility does hold a Department registration, so the same duty reaches that operator.
verification_notes: Read in the official 105 CMR 700.001 and 105 CMR 700.004(A), read with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 7(a) on malegislature.gov text published at mass.gov on 2026-09-11. Added as a new rule so that no released adjudication is disturbed. A fresh independent audit is still required before any section relying on it is published.
